group_assessment.weighting: An orthopaedic surgery and pathology group at one Indian centre using WWOX and RUNX2 as tumour biomarkers in a seven-patient pilot; not a WWOX group and not a neurological-disease group. Observation (IHC scores, a Kaplan-Meier curve) is weighted above interpretation (RUNX2 as prognostic biomarker), which the data cannot carry at this size, and the survival statistics are internally inconsistent.

entries.proposition: WWOX protein by IHC does NOT differ between seven Ewing sarcoma cases and five controls (medians about 204 versus 197, P = 0.876); RUNX2 is higher in cases (about 238 versus 155, P = 0.005). The record's title wording ('intertwined relationship ... biomarker for predicting response') is not what the data show: no WWOX difference, no WWOX-RUNX2 correlation reported, no response endpoint.
entries.snippet: In Table 2, the median expression levels of WWOX did not exhibit a statistically significant difference between the cases (203.78; range: 151.89-237.61) and the controls (197.02; range: 157.86-241.34; p = 0.876).

entries.proposition: Figure 2 (hand reading): the curve steps from 100% to about 86% (month 3), 71% (month 6), 43% (month 8) and 29% (month 29) and then plateaus at about 29% to month 50, with numbers at risk 7, 3, 3, 2, 1, 1. The median (the time the curve crosses 50%) is about 8 months, not 45; the plateau at 29% implies two censored patients, whereas Table 1 and the text give six deaths and one survivor (a plateau would then be 14%, or the curve ends at zero). Caption, table and curve cannot all be right. No survival is stratified by WWOX or RUNX2 level.
